newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia 96/97 wheat imports down 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia 96/97 wheat imports down 50 pct.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA'S WHEAT IMPORTS OVER 1996/97 SEEN 1.5 MILLION TONNES; EXPORTS SEEN 0.6 MILLION TONNES
MOSCOW, July 1 - SovEcon's estimate for Russia's wheat imports (not including wheat flour) in 1996/97 is 1.55 million tonnes, which is about 50 percent down on the previous season.
The decline mainly comes from increased wheat production in 1996 and constrained domestic demand.
Russia has significantly boosted its wheat exports this season. But it remained in 1996/97 a net wheat importer of about one million tonnes.
Due to the improved outlook for wheat output in 1997/98, Russia may further increase its wheat exports and reduce its imports, reaching a zero balance in its wheat trade.
Wheat imports in April peaked at nearly 230,000 tonnes on the back of tight stocks.
In May, the imports declined but remained relatively high at 180,000 tonnes. Nearly all imported wheat was delivered from Kazakhstan.
Kazakh wheat deliveries have accounted for the bulk of wheat offers on the domestic market since April.
Feed wheat makes up the bulk of Russian wheat exports, particularly to non-Commonwealth of Independent States countries.

However, with the start of a Russian-Uzbek barter deal involving Russian milling wheat for Uzbek cotton, Russia has increased its milling wheat exports to Uzbekistan. The wheat is delivered from Western Siberia where it is bought with fuel and lubricants supplied the Neftyanoi company, which is in charge of the deal.

However, reduced marketable wheat stocks are likely to limit wheat deliveries to Uzbekistan. The barter deal will not reach its target of 300,000 tonnes of wheat before July 1, 1997 as requested by the Uzbek government.
